case: index 83 gci_C alpha 0, ANK only, L2 1e-6, idle 6-core host
why: the earlier test (AUDIT C8) fixed the cycle budget, which measures throughput, not time to an answer
finding: time to the answer does keep improving past 2 ranks: 2.56x on 6 ranks (43 % efficiency), 1.89x on 2 (95 %), 2.50x on 4 (62 %). The fixed-budget test's 'flat beyond 2 ranks' was an artefact of that test, not the solver
cost: core-hours per point rise with rank count: 0.59, 0.62, 0.94, 1.38. A rented machine is paid for whole, so the cheapest batch runs MANY CASES AT ONCE with 2-4 ranks each, not one case on all cores; concurrency is then limited by memory, about 18.6 GiB per gci_F case
